title: Integrated Landscape Visual Quality Index (IVQI): Methodological Integration of Visual Perception Analysis and Landscape Metrics
content: Assessing the visual quality of a landscape has long been split across two methodological traditions: perceptual models, which reproduce human visual experience through three-dimensional visibility algorithms from an egocentric viewpoint, and objective models, which describe landscape structure through multidimensional metrics from an exocentric viewpoint. This separation has created a methodological gap hindering a comprehensive assessment of the landscape as a whole. This study introduces the Integrated Visual Quality Index (IVQI), which integrates the visual-perception algorithm of He et al. and the multidimensional landscape-quality indicator system of Sowińska-Świerkosz and Michalik-Śnieżek . The IVQI retains the additive structure and range of values of the original model (yielding a continuous index in the range [1, 10]), while expanding its resource quality component (R) into a weighted sum of eleven standardized indicators, grouped into four dimensions (structural, ecological, cultural, and visual) weighted using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). For each visible cell, a visual perception component (P) is added, based on distance and horizontal and vertical viewing angles. The result is a spatially explicit and replicable instrument that articulates egocentric and exocentric perspectives and provides urban planners with a tool to identify priority areas for landscape intervention or conservation.
